chapters.title: David's lament
chapters.summary: A man brings news of Saul's death and claims to have killed him. David mourns with a song for Saul and Jonathan: how are the mighty fallen.

chapters.title: David king of Judah
chapters.summary: David is anointed king over Judah at Hebron, while Saul's son Ish-bosheth rules the north. War breaks out between the two houses.

chapters.title: Abner killed
chapters.summary: Abner, Saul's general, defects to David, but Joab murders him in revenge. David mourns him publicly.

chapters.title: Ish-bosheth murdered
chapters.summary: Two men murder Ish-bosheth in his bed and bring his head to David, who executes them for killing an innocent man.

chapters.title: Jerusalem the city of David
chapters.summary: All Israel anoints David king. He captures Jerusalem from the Jebusites and makes it his capital, and defeats the Philistines twice.

chapters.title: The ark comes to Jerusalem
chapters.summary: Uzzah dies touching the ark. Later David brings it into Jerusalem with joy, dancing before the Lord with all his might. Michal despises him.

chapters.title: God's covenant with David
chapters.summary: David wants to build God a house, but God promises instead to build David a house: a lasting dynasty and a throne established forever. David prays in wonder.

chapters.title: David's victories
chapters.summary: God gives David victory over Philistia, Moab, Zobah, Aram and Edom. David reigns with justice and fairness for all his people.

chapters.title: Kindness to Mephibosheth
chapters.summary: For Jonathan's sake, David shows kindness to Jonathan's lame son Mephibosheth, restoring his land and giving him a place at the king's table.

chapters.title: War with Ammon
chapters.summary: The Ammonites humiliate David's envoys and hire Aramean troops. Joab and Abishai defeat them.

chapters.title: David and Bathsheba
chapters.summary: While his army is at war, David takes Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah. When she conceives, he arranges for Uriah to be killed in battle. The thing displeased the Lord.

chapters.title: Thou art the man
chapters.summary: The prophet Nathan tells a parable that exposes David's sin. David confesses and is forgiven, but the child dies. Later Solomon is born.

chapters.title: Amnon and Tamar
chapters.summary: David's son Amnon rapes his half-sister Tamar. Her brother Absalom waits two years and then has Amnon killed, and flees.

chapters.title: Absalom returns
chapters.summary: Joab uses a wise woman's story to persuade David to bring Absalom home, but David refuses to see him for two years.

chapters.title: Absalom's revolt
chapters.summary: Absalom steals the hearts of Israel and declares himself king at Hebron. David flees Jerusalem weeping, sending the ark back and trusting God.

chapters.title: Ziba and Shimei
chapters.summary: As David flees, Ziba brings supplies and slanders his master. Shimei curses David, who refuses to retaliate. Absalom takes his father's concubines.

chapters.title: Conflicting counsel
chapters.summary: Absalom follows Hushai's advice over Ahithophel's, as God had planned. David is warned and crosses the Jordan, and loyal friends bring food.

chapters.title: O Absalom, my son
chapters.summary: David's forces defeat Absalom's army in the forest. Absalom is caught in a tree and killed by Joab. David weeps: would God I had died for thee.

chapters.title: David returns
chapters.summary: Joab rebukes David for mourning instead of thanking his men. David returns, pardons Shimei, hears Mephibosheth, and Judah and Israel argue over the king.

chapters.title: Sheba's rebellion
chapters.summary: Sheba leads the northern tribes away from David. Joab murders Amasa, besieges Sheba in Abel, and a wise woman ends the siege.

chapters.title: Famine and giants
chapters.summary: A famine is linked to Saul's wrong against the Gibeonites and ends after his descendants are handed over. David's men defeat Philistine giants.

chapters.title: David's song of deliverance
chapters.summary: David sings of God as his rock, fortress and deliverer, who drew him out of many waters and rewarded his faithfulness.

chapters.title: David's last words
chapters.summary: David's final words describe a just ruler like morning light and God's everlasting covenant. A list of his mighty men and their deeds follows.

chapters.title: The census and the altar
chapters.summary: David sins by counting his fighting men, and a plague follows. He buys Araunah's threshing floor for an altar, refusing to offer what cost him nothing.
